subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should GatewayClient keep unlimited reconnects by default and expose only an opt-in cap for short-lived callers, or should OpenClaw change the default reconnect policy globally?
rationale: The unbounded scheduler is source-reproducible, but node-host recovery relies on indefinite reconnects, so the default retry contract is a compatibility and product decision.

options.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
options.body: Keep existing long-lived clients unlimited by default, add the cap to the package client, and wire it only into short-lived caller paths maintainers approve.

options.title: Global retry cap
options.body: Stop every GatewayClient after a fixed number of attempts, accepting that node hosts may not recover automatically after extended gateway outages.

options.title: Document unlimited retry
options.body: Keep the current retry model and close the report only if maintainers explicitly accept the resource-risk tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
recommendation.body: Keep existing long-lived clients unlimited by default, add the cap to the package client, and wire it only into short-lived caller paths maintainers approve.

likelyOwner.reason: The original Gateway WebSocket control plane and package extraction history make this the best available owner for the reconnect contract decision.
